motivation: In 2007 Lorimer, Bailes and McLaughlin found a single, intensely bright millisecond radio burst in archival Parkes pulsar-survey data. Its dispersion measure placed it far beyond the Milky Way. This 'Lorimer burst' revealed an entirely new class of cosmic phenomenon. The discovery rested on McLaughlin's earlier development of single-pulse search techniques, with which she also discovered rotating radio transients. Fast radio bursts are now detected by the thousands. They have been localized to host galaxies, and one has been tied to a Galactic magnetar. They act as unique probes of baryons in the intergalactic medium, used to solve the 'missing baryon' problem, and they test plasma physics, magnetism and coherent emission under extreme conditions. Few discoveries since pulsars have opened such a rich new window on the transient Universe. The nominees' insight, persistence and methods founded a field that now engages observatories worldwide.
